title: Entity
description: An actor in the crisis world. Four kinds: information_source (emits signals, cannot act), authority (decides and orders; the system contacts it), responder (acts on the ground with finite units), population (aggregate of civilians per zone; what the system protects).

id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier. Referenced by signals, actions, and escalation chains.

name.description: Human-readable name. Used verbatim in voice calls and dashboard labels.

kind.description: Role of the entity. information_source: only emits signals. authority: can order high-level actions (alerts, evacuations, road closures). responder: executes physical actions with finite units. population: civilian aggregate per zone; the protection target.

weight.description: Authority prior, 1-10. Tiebreaker for who is notified first and whose orders take precedence. Does not replace jurisdiction: an entity with weight 7 and jurisdiction [paiporta] has no authority in torrent.

trust.description: Prior reliability of what this entity reports. A starting point only: per-signal confidence (computed from corroboration, consistency, and age) is what decisions must use. Runtime evidence can downgrade this prior via the update_entity action.

jurisdiction.description: Zone ids where this entity can act or give orders. Empty array means global jurisdiction.

channel.description: How the system contacts this entity for real. kind none for entities never contacted (sensors, media).

kind.description: Contact channel. voice: real phone call through HappyRobot. email and sms: real messages. none: not contactable.

address.description: Phone number, email address, or broadcast target (broadcast:<zone> for population mass alerts).

capabilities.description: Action verbs this entity can execute. The agent must never assign an action outside this list. Examples: send_es_alert, order_evacuation, close_road, rescue, pump_water, shelter, supplies, wellness_check.

units.description: Countable resources, only for responders. Scarcity of units is what forces prioritization.

available.description: Units not currently assigned. The simulator and actions update this.

population.description: Only for kind population. The civilian state of a zone.

warned.description: True after a mass alert or evacuation order reaches this zone.

at_risk_pct.description: Share (0-100) in dangerous places (garages, ground floors, vehicles). The main harm driver: warnings and evacuations reduce it. Minimizing this is the system objective.

activation.description: What it takes to make this entity operational.

delay_min.description: Minutes from request to operational. Long delays (UME: 180) force early requests on incomplete evidence.

cost.description: Political or economic cost of activation. high-cost actions require human approval on the dashboard before execution.

escalation_to.description: Entity id to contact when this entity is unreachable. null means top of the chain.

zone.description: Current zone id of the entity. null or absent for entities without a physical position. remote for responders outside the map.

status.description: Operational state. The simulator can change it mid-run (entities go unreachable during the crisis); the agent must then use escalation_to.

provenance.description: plan: pre-registered in the scenario pack (the official emergency plan). discovered: created at runtime by the register_entity action when signals reveal a new actor. Discovered entities start with trust low and only low-risk capabilities until a human upgrades them.

notes.description: Free-text context about this entity, injected into agent prompts. Use it for operational constraints (Do not send volunteers into active hazard zones) and background.
